source: No exam-archive or worksheet source — originally-authored content, per user-provided question framework (2026-08-20)
background: Confirmed no exam-archive-quality source exists for rivers/mountains/capitals at grade 3-5 (see research/source_catalog.md 2026-08-18 verdict). This round did a deeper live re-check before falling back to original authorship: TeachersPayTeachers free-tier Geography category was pulled live (bypassing the site's 403-to-bots block via a browser user-agent) across all three target grades (3rd/4th/5th) and both Worksheets and Assessment resource types — 6 category pages, ~70 unique free products, zero rivers/mountains/world-capitals MC quizzes among them; the one MC world-capitals quiz found with an answer key was a paid $3.75 item for grades 8-11. Also checked and ruled out: National Geographic GeoBee (quiz-bowl format, all-rights-reserved IP, wrong difficulty tier), UK KS2 (no standalone geography SATs exist), Texas STAAR World Geography (high-school course, same age-mismatch as the already-used Virginia SOL source).
authorship: All facts below are well-established, easily independently verifiable geography facts (national capitals, longest rivers/tallest mountains per continent, well-known desert/plain facts) — not copied from or closely paraphrased from any single source. Several less-common facts (Danube's country count, Amazon's name origin, Atacama as driest place, Pampas/Serengeti/North European Plain locations) were spot-verified via web search during authoring; sources are noted per-item in the authoring notes below, not carried into the seed file itself.
images: 12 new map images added under public/images/geography/map-shaded-<country>.png — orthographic-projection globe views with one country highlighted in green, sourced from Wikimedia Commons (the same 'X (orthographic projection).svg' file series already used across Wikipedia country infoboxes). All verified individually for license (public domain or CC BY / CC BY-SA / dual GFDL+CC, all permissive) and author; see public/images/CREDITS.md for the full per-file attribution table. Argentina's version of this file series includes a shaded Antarctic-claim wedge that would be confusing/inaccurate for a simple 'name this country' question aimed at a 9-year-old, so Argentina was dropped from the country list in favor of South Africa (a clean single landmass) after visually inspecting the downloaded image.
factual_spot_checks: Amazon River name origin (Francisco de Orellana, 1542, named after Greek Amazons after reported battles with female warriors) — confirmed via multiple sources including Britannica.
Danube flows through ~10 countries (Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova, Ukraine) — confirmed via Britannica/worldatlas.
Atacama Desert (Chile) is the driest place on Earth outside the poles — confirmed via multiple sources including ESA and HowStuffWorks.

South Africa was deliberately NOT used for a 'what is the capital' question — it has three capitals (Pretoria/Cape Town/Bloemfontein), which is too ambiguous for a simple single-answer MC item at this age band. Used only for a 'name the country' map question instead.
status: 34 items authored (12 map-based capitals/countries, 22 text-based rivers/mountains/deserts/plains facts). Staged in staging.json / staging-geography.json — NOT YET MERGED into data/seed/geography.json. Per pipeline design, nothing merges until human review and explicit sign-off.
